sources.entry: Tasks.md - A self-hosted, file based task management board that supports Markdown syntax. MIT Docker

summary.one_liner: Tasks.md is a self-hosted task management board where lanes, cards and tags are stored as plain Markdown files on disk, run mainly via a single Docker image.
summary.what_it_does: It provides a responsive web board for creating cards, lanes and tags, with each card written as a Markdown file. Every lane is a directory in the filesystem and every task is a file, so the data stays readable outside the app. It offers light and dark themes that follow the operating system, plus three built-in color themes (Adwaita, Nord, Catppuccin) and custom CSS overrides via a custom.css file. It supports running under a subpath reverse proxy through a BASE_PATH variable, can be installed as a PWA, and includes multilingual support with browser-based locale detection. A background cleanup removes local images no longer referenced by any task, on a configurable interval.
use_cases: self-hosted kanban board for personal to-dos
managing tasks as Markdown files on disk
team task lanes behind a reverse proxy
keeping project tasks alongside Obsidian notes
customizing a task board's look with CSS themes
how_to_run: docker run -d --name tasks.md -e PUID=1000 -e PGID=1000 -p 8080:8080 -v /path/to/tasks/:/tasks/ -v /path/to/config/:/config/ --restart unless-stopped baldissaramatheus/tasks.md
Alternatively, use the docker-compose example in the README with image baldissaramatheus/tasks.md, mapping /tasks and /config volumes and port 8080.
Source install: git clone --recursive the repo, then run npm install and npm start in both the /frontend and /backend directories.
Optional environment variables: TITLE, BASE_PATH, LOCAL_IMAGES_CLEANUP_INTERVAL (set to 0 to disable cleanup).
notable: Tasks are plain Markdown files and lanes are directories, so data is portable and works with Obsidian
Single Docker image install with PUID/PGID support for file ownership
Three default color themes plus full CSS color-variable customization
Subpath reverse-proxy support and installable as a PWA
Automatic cleanup of unused local images
caveats: PWA does not work when BASE_PATH is set to anything other than "/"
Upgrading from version 2.x to 3.x requires extra steps described in the README
The README describes the project as low maintenance, with a deliberately narrow feature scope
